findings.claim: How media products reach audiences through online, physical, and broadcast distribution platforms.
findings.truth: The spec sets three categories: online (apps, multimedia, web), physical platforms (computer, interactive tv, kiosks, mobile devices) and physical media (CD/DVD, memory stick, paper based). Broadcast is not one of them and the lesson never teaches it.

findings.claim: The OCR specification identifies three main categories of distribution
findings.truth: Student-facing text must not name the exam board. The three categories themselves are correct.
findings.evidence: house rule for this vocational qualification; spec 4.1

findings.claim: over 60% of global internet traffic now comes from mobile devices
findings.truth: No settled figure supports this. Statcounter (August 2026) puts mobile at 49.36% of global page views, desktop 49.11%. The statistic is dropped; the claim that mobile is the most used platform stands.

findings.claim: Images for a website should be saved as JPEG or PNG at 72 DPI (and the matching knowledge check: 'saved at _____ DPI')
findings.truth: Screen resolution is measured in PPI; DPI is the printed measure. Lesson 2 teaches exactly that split, so the unit contradicted itself. Fixed in both the content and knowledge check 4 (answer 72 unchanged).
findings.evidence: spec 4.2.1 'Know what is meant by DPI/PPI'; lesson 2 key fact

findings.claim: In the R093 exam, questions on distribution platforms often appear in Section B
findings.truth: The unit code must not appear in student-facing text. The Section B claim itself is right: Section B is the context-based section and samples every topic area.
findings.evidence: spec R093 assessment guidance (Section A 10 marks, Section B 60 marks, 1h30, 70 marks)

findings.claim: 'Explain one advantage ...' labelled 4 marks, with a scheme that awards 2 marks per developed advantage
findings.truth: One advantage can only reach 2 marks under its own scheme. The stem now asks for two advantages and the scheme header says 2 marks per advantage, matching the 4-mark pattern used in lesson 4.
findings.evidence: the question's own mark scheme; lesson 4 practice question 4

findings.claim: 'QWC: specialist terminology used accurately' in the 8-mark band descriptor (all four lessons)
findings.truth: The spec's assessment guidance carries no quality-of-written-communication or SPaG marks. The band still rewards accurate specialist terminology, so only the QWC label is removed.
findings.evidence: spec R093 assessment guidance; no QWC/SPaG anywhere in the spec

findings.claim: Card 4: answer 'Distribution' for the cloze '_____ refers to the methods used to deliver media products ...'
findings.truth: The answer duplicated card 1 ('distribution') and was a one-word cloze. Replaced with an interactive TV card taught in the lesson; every answer in the deck is now unique.
findings.evidence: flashcard validator rules (duplicate answers, one-word cloze)

findings.claim: Pixels, resolution, DPI vs PPI, colour depth, bitmap vs vector, and image file formats explained.
findings.truth: Colour depth is a R094 graphics property, not an exam topic-area-4 image property, and the lesson never explains it. The description now lists what the lesson actually teaches.
findings.evidence: spec 4.2.1 (DPI/PPI, pixel dimension only); spec 2.2 of R094 lists colour depth

findings.claim: PNG ... Standard web resolution is 96 PPI.
findings.truth: A PPI value is metadata, not a property of the PNG format, and 96 contradicts the 72 PPI web figure the same lesson teaches for JPEG and in its key fact. Sentence removed.

findings.claim: A common exam question asks: 'What type of images maintain exactly the same quality regardless of how much the image size is increased?' (repeated as practice question 4)
findings.truth: The lesson presents this as a board exam question in quotation marks. Reworded in house vocabulary in both places; the taught answer (vector images) is unchanged.

findings.claim: Cards 4 and 5: 'PPI _____ Per Inch) refers to ...' / 'DPI _____ Per Inch) refers to ...', answers 'Pixels' and 'Dots'
findings.truth: Both were mangled clozes cut from the body text (the opening bracket is missing), both answers appear in their own question, and 'Pixels' duplicated card 1. Replaced with a bitmap card and a GIF card, both taught in the lesson.

findings.claim: OGG Vorbis ... No licensing fees, unlike MP3.
findings.truth: MP3 patents have expired (EU by 2012, the last US patent on 16 April 2017), so MP3 carries no licence fee either. The OGG claim is now stated without the comparison.

findings.claim: Card 4: one-word answer 'Nyquist' to a cloze that ends '... this is known as the _____ theorem'
findings.truth: A one-word answer needs a question that asks for the name. Reworded as 'Name the theorem ...'; the physics in the card is correct (sample rate at least double the highest frequency).
findings.evidence: flashcard validator rules; lesson content on the Nyquist theorem

findings.claim: AVI (.avi) ... An older, typically uncompressed video format that produces very high quality.
findings.truth: AVI is a container that can carry almost any compression scheme (uncompressed full frame, Indeo, run-length, Microsoft Video 1 and others); most AVI files are compressed. Reworded to 'often holds video with little or no compression'.

findings.claim: The specification requires you to know five resolution standards: (followed by four headings)
findings.truth: The spec names five: SD, HD, UHD, 4K, 8K. The lesson merges UHD and 4K into one heading, so a student counts four. The five are now named in the sentence.

findings.claim: Card 4: 'HD (High _____ - 1280 x 720 pixels ...' with the answer 'Definition'
findings.truth: A mangled cloze cut from the body text, with an answer that teaches nothing. Replaced with 'What do the letters HD stand for in video resolution?' / 'High Definition'.
findings.evidence: flashcard validator rules; spec 4.2.3 'Know what is meant by SD, HD, UHD, 4K, 8K'

findings.claim: Card 5: cloze '_____ is the most widely used resolution for online video today', answer '1080p'
findings.truth: A one-word cloze answer needs a question that asks for it. Reworded as 'Which resolution ...'; the answer is unchanged.

findings.claim: TIFF ... Produces very high-quality images at 300 DPI
findings.truth: 300 DPI is the print target, not a property of TIFF. The sentence reads as a typical print use, so it is left alone; the JPEG '72 PPI for web' figure is kept for the same reason (it is the board's teaching convention, although a PPI value does not change how a browser displays an image).

findings.claim: Practice question 1 credits 'Colour depth' as a property of a digital image file
findings.truth: Colour depth is a R094 property, not one of the two the exam lists for static images (DPI/PPI resolution, pixel dimension). It is still a real property and would be credited, so the accept list is left alone.

findings.claim: Practice question 1 credits 'Aspect ratio' as a property of a moving image file
findings.truth: The exam lists frame rate and resolution for moving image files; aspect ratio appears only in the NEA video units. Harmless in an accept list, so no edit.

findings.claim: WebM ... Uses both lossy and lossless compression.
findings.truth: WebM's normal web codecs (VP8/VP9 video, Vorbis/Opus audio) are lossy; only VP9 has a rarely used lossless mode. Too marginal for the exam to edit.

findings.claim: A video at 60 fps ... the file will be approximately twice as large [as 30 fps]
findings.truth: True for uncompressed video. With the inter-frame compression MP4/H.264 uses, doubling the frame rate typically adds far less than double the data. The simplification is the one the board teaches, so no edit.

findings.claim: 'questions ... often appear in Section B'
findings.truth: Kept. There is one exam paper with a Section A and a Section B, both named in the spec, so this is not a 'Paper 1 Section B' style code.

summary: Four lessons checked against R093 topic area 4. No HIGH findings: every technical value (44.1 kHz, 16/24-bit level counts, 3-minute WAV at about 30 MB, MP3 at roughly a tenth, SD/HD/4K/8K pixel counts, disc capacities, 6-megapixel arithmetic, Nyquist) recomputes or verifies correctly, and all 20 knowledge-check answer keys are right. The fixes are 24 findings / 29 edits: two student-facing board and unit-code mentions, an unsupported mobile-traffic statistic, a DPI/PPI contradiction between lessons 1 and 2, an invented '96 PPI' PNG property, AVI described as uncompressed, an out-of-date MP3 licensing claim, a 4-mark question whose scheme could only reach 2, a quoted exam question removed for copyright distancing, four QWC labels the spec does not support, and six broken or duplicated flashcards.
